issues.area: concurrency / R-SYN-15 (MUST): the memory-pressure observer outlives shutdown() while the engine is still `created` (new this round)
issues.location: Two facade paths reach it. (1) Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/AssetClient.swift:358-364 and :417-425: register(_:) → apply(.start) → ClientLifecycle.observeMemoryPressure → self.core.engine.observeMemoryPressure at Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/ClientLifecycle.swift:317. Nothing requires start() first. (2) ClientLifecycle.swift:201-205: performReopen applies the recorded request to the `created` replacement before `next.engine.start()` at :224. In both cases ClientLifecycle.shutdown() (:238-253) then shuts down an engine that is still `created`. The root cause is in WP-F's files: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineLifecycle.swift:466-470. The `.created` branch of performShutdown sets shuttingDown and calls finishShutdown without cancelling or joining state.tasks. Meanwhile EngineCommands.swift:1134-1154 (performObserveMemoryPressure) spawns the `.pressure` owned task in `created`, which spawn allows (EngineLifecycle.swift:52-58).
issues.problem: After AssetClient.shutdown(), or after AssetClient.deinit's shutdown, the engine is `.shutDown` but still owns a live observer task. That task holds a live memory-pressure subscription. It ends only at the next memory-pressure event, when its loop finally sees the shutdown. spawn's closure captures the engine, so until then the task keeps the engine, store and environment alive. R-SYN-15 requires 'shutdown() cancels all tasks … tests prove no task leaks'; AssetClient.shutdown()'s own doc says 'Cancels every task'. PROVEN with a scratch copy of the tree (.build-verify-g-correct-r3/probes/pkg, worktree untouched). PROBE-1: register a cache before start, then shutdown. Output: 'before: lifecycle=created ownedTasks=1 observer=true; after: lifecycle=shutDown ownedTasks=1 observer=true liveObservations=1'. The observer went away only after one more pressure event ('liveObservations=0 purges=0'). Control, register after start: 'after: lifecycle=shutDown ownedTasks=0 observer=false'. PROBE-2 covers the reopen path. A probe-only seam point sits right after the replacement's pressure request, which is exactly where the shipped code goes on to start(); it changes no logic. Output: 'generation=1 before shutdown: lifecycle=created ownedTasks=1 observer=true; after: lifecycle=shutDown ownedTasks=1 observer=true liveObservations=1; purge=failure(shutDown)'. The same branch also lets a joinGroup task, spawned by a prefetch made before start, run after shutdown returns (briefly).
issues.fix: The orchestrator rules on a contract change request to WP-F, as for CCR-G2. The change: the `.created` branch of performShutdown cancels every owned task, calls resumeEverything(with: .shutDown) and joins the tasks with the same loop the other branches use, then calls finishShutdown. I validated this change in the probe copy. PROBE-1 and PROBE-2 then pass ('after: lifecycle=shutDown ownedTasks=0 observer=false liveObservations=0'). ZTronAssetSyncTests passed 305 of 305, and the Kit tests all passed with the same 4 CCR-G2 known issues. WP-G's part: (a) add a regression test in PROBE-1's shape to FacadeLifecycleTests or FacadeRaceTests: register before start, then shutdown, then assert introspect().ownedTasks == 0, memoryPressureObserverActive == false and pressure.activeObservers == 0. (b) Optionally, in performReopen, apply the recorded pressure request after `next.engine.start()` rather than before it, so a reopen never starts an observer on a `created` engine. (c) Note the facade-only stopgap and its limit: a newer-epoch stop before the engine's shutdown cancels the observer but cannot join it, so the guarantee needs the engine change.

issues.area: events / R-SYN-12 (MUST: 'terminal events never dropped'): a client stream follows a reopen only after the replacement has started, and drops the replacement's terminal events (new this round)
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/EventForwarder.swift:166-169: the pump switches engines through lifecycle.current(), then registers through makeEventStream(), which registers on its first pull. Sources/ZTronAssetKit/Facade/ClientLifecycle.swift:132-138: current() waits for the whole reopen task (`await reopening.value`). That task's value arrives only after group re-registration (:206-218) and `await next.engine.start()` (:224), although the replacement is installed much earlier, at endReopen(next) (:200). The engine's replay, Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineEvents.swift:108-132, repeats snapshot, conditions and run state only.
issues.problem: Take a consumer that holds `events` or a `subscribe()` stream through a B-15 reopen. Suppose the pump asked for the current pair before endReopen. This is the common case: the retired engine's clientShutDown reaches the pump while the reopen is still in its main-actor hop to reset the mirror. That consumer never receives the terminal events the replacement publishes between its installation and the end of performReopen. The replacement's `clientStarted(generation:)` ('Terminal: start() finished and the first snapshot is installed') is always among them. The same goes for `assetAvailable`, `assetFailed` and similar events from callers that reach the replacement after endReopen, or from re-registered prefetch groups. PROVEN in the scratch copy. PROBE-3 registers the consumer before start, then reopens through purge(.all). Result: 'the replacement's clientStarted was missing in 20 of 20 rounds'; after the switch the consumer got only the replay. PROBE-4 uses a prefetch group so the reopen parks at the shipped `registrationAnswered` seam point, then runs resolve("x") on the replacement while it is parked; a direct subscriber of the replacement, registered before the resolve, is the control. In the 2 of 4 runs where the pump had not yet followed (subscribersWhileParked=0), the consumer never received assetAvailable(x) ('received=false'). In the one of those runs with the control, the control printed 'the direct subscriber of the replacement saw assetAvailable(x): true'. In the 2 runs where the pump had already followed, the event arrived.
issues.fix: Make the forwarder follow the replacement as soon as it is installed. For example, current() could wait only until the running reopen installs its pair or ends without one: continuations stored by current() and resumed in endReopen, instead of `await reopening.value`; reopen(replacing:) keeps awaiting the task. I validated exactly this change in the probe copy. PROBE-3 then missed the event in 0 of 20 rounds and PROBE-4 printed 'received=true'. All 67 original Kit tests passed in 3 of 3 runs, with the same 4 CCR-G2 known issues; the G-12 and shutdown-during-reopen tests passed too. Add a regression test in PROBE-3's shape to FacadeReopenTests: consumer registered before start, reopen, then assert the replacement's clientStarted (or a terminal asset event) arrives. PROBE-3 fails deterministically today. Update g-1's REENTRANCY row to say the wait ends at install. If the design means to hide the replacement's clientStarted, as it hides the retired clientShutDown, filter it explicitly and say so in G-2; asset events must still arrive.
